chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Ali ibn al-Hakam from al-'Ala' from Muhammad ibn Muslim from one of them (peace be upon them both): Concerning a man who bequeathed his wealth in the way of Allah.
He said: 'Give to those he bequeathed to, even if they are Jewish or Christian.'
Indeed, Allah the Exalted says: 'So whoever alters the bequest after he has heard it, then the sin is only upon those who alter it. Indeed, Allah is Hearing and Knowing.'
ai.seo_question: Can a Muslim bequeath their wealth to non-Muslims in the way of Allah?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration to clarify that a bequest to *Ahl al-Kitab* (Jews and Christians) is legally valid and enforceable, provided the testator's intent is preserved. The citation of Surah Al-Baqarah 2:181 underscores the principle that the sin of deviation rests solely on those who alter the will, thereby validating the original designation regardless of the beneficiaries' faith. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic view that the validity of the *wasiyyah* (bequest) is not contingent upon the religious identity of the heir, but rather on the fidelity to the testator's explicit instructions.
